review_candidates.title: General Manager -Transmission Line
review_candidates.description: The General Manager – Transmission Line will be responsible for establishing, leading, and managing the organization’s Transmission Line function. The role will have end-to-end accountability for the planning, development, engineering, approvals, procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover of high-voltage transmission line projects. The position will provide strategic, technical, commercial, and operational leadership to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and within approved scope, quality, schedule, and budget , while maintaining compliance with applicable laws, regulations, grid codes, and national/international standards. 2. Key Responsibilities A. Strategic Leadership & Department Management Establish, structure, and operationalize the Transmission Line division. Develop and implement transmission project strategies aligned with organizational objectives. Provide strategic advice and regular project updates to the CEO and Board on technical, commercial, financial, and operational matters. Lead and develop a high-performing multidisciplinary project team. Establish a culture of safety, accountability, quality, performance, and timely project delivery. B. Project Development & Planning Lead transmission projects from initial concept, route alignment, surveys, and feasibility through to commissioning and final handover. Oversee route studies, technical feasibility, geotechnical investigations, survey mapping, and route optimization. Develop and maintain Master Project Execution Plans, baseline schedules, budgets, and project control systems. Identify critical-path issues and implement mitigation and recovery measures. Ensure effective coordination between transmission infrastructure and associated generation/substation facilities. C. Engineering & Technical Management Provide overall technical leadership for transmission line engineering and execution. Oversee tower design, structural configuration, foundation engineering, conductor and OPGW selection, insulation, earthing, protection, SCADA, and related systems. Review and drive design optimization and value engineering while maintaining safety, reliability, and technical integrity. Ensure technical coordination across substations, switchyards, generating stations, and grid interfaces. Manage engineering consultants, specialist design firms, and technical audit agencies. Ensure compliance with applicable IEC, IEEE, national grid codes, and other relevant technical standards. D. Grid Interconnection & Power Evacuation Lead technical and commercial coordination with electricity utilities, grid authorities, and relevant stakeholders for grid interconnection. Ensure compliance with grid-code requirements, protection systems, metering, and SCADA interfaces. Oversee grid inspections, pre-commissioning testing, energization, synchronization, and related procedures. Coordinate transmission-line completion with generation and substation readiness to support timely power evacuation. E. Statutory Approvals & Government Relations Lead the acquisition and management of all required statutory approvals, permits, and clearances. Coordinate with relevant federal, provincial, and local government authorities. Manage engagement with energy authorities, electricity departments, forest authorities, regulators, and other statutory bodies. Maintain a comprehensive regulatory and statutory compliance tracker and ensure timely renewals and closures. F. Right-of-Way, Land Acquisition & Stakeholder Management Lead ROW clearance, tower-footprint acquisition, substation land acquisition, and access arrangements. Oversee land ownership verification, valuation, compensation, negotiations, and settlements. Maintain effective relationships with local authorities, communities, landowners, and other stakeholders. Manage forest clearances, compensatory afforestation requirements, and public-land lease processes. Proactively address social and access-related issues that may affect project timelines. G. Procurement & Supply Chain Management Develop appropriate procurement and contracting strategies, including EPC and split-contract models. Lead preparation of technical specifications, tender documents, bid evaluations, and vendor negotiations. Oversee procurement of major transmission components including towers, conductors, insulators, hardware, and associated equipment. Manage local and international supply-chain activities, including factory acceptance testing, transportation, logistics, and site material management. H. Contract & Commercial Management Oversee EPC, construction, consultancy, and other project-related contracts. Ensure compliance with contractual, technical, commercial, and performance requirements. Manage variations, change orders, extension-of-time claims, and contractual negotiations. Monitor commercial risks, performance guarantees, letters of credit, liquidated damages, warranties, and other contractual obligations. I. Construction & Project Execution Provide leadership and oversight for civil works, access roads, foundations, tower erection, conductor stringing, and associated transmission-line construction activities. Oversee execution in challenging terrain, including mountainous areas, river crossings, and remote locations. Monitor contractor productivity, resource deployment, work schedules, and performance. Ensure appropriate planning for adverse terrain, slope stability, monsoon conditions, and remote-site logistics. J. Health, Safety, Environment & Quality Establish and enforce comprehensive HSEQ standards across all project sites. Drive QA/QC systems covering civil, structural, electrical, and transmission-line works. Promote a strong safety culture and maintain a zero-harm approach. Ensure compliance with environmental requirements, social safeguards, and site restoration obligations. K. Risk, Budget & Project Governance Develop and maintain the project Master Risk Register covering technical, commercial, geological, environmental, and regulatory risks. Prepare and monitor project CAPEX, cash-flow forecasts, and budgets. Implement effective cost-control mechanisms to minimize budget overruns. Monitor project KPIs, milestones, risks, and overall performance. Provide regular management reports, dashboards, and executive-level project updates. 3. Required Qualifications & Experience Education Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical & Electronics Engineering, Civil Engineering , or a related discipline from a recognized institution. Master’s degree in Power Systems, Engineering Management, MBA , or a related field will be an advantage. Professional registration/license with the relevant Engineering Council is required. Mandatory Experience 7–10 years of progressive experience in senior leadership roles within transmission-line projects. Proven experience delivering at least one 132kV or higher greenfield transmission-line project from concept through commissioning . Strong experience working with government authorities, utilities, regulators, consultants, contractors, and local communities. Proven experience managing EPC contractors and multidisciplinary engineering/project teams. Demonstrated track record of delivering complex infrastructure projects within approved budgets and schedules. Preferred Experience Experience in power evacuation and transmission systems . Experience working on projects in mountainous, remote, or challenging terrain . Experience with donor-funded or internationally financed infrastructure projects . 4. Key Competencies Technical Expertise: Strong knowledge of 132kV/220kV/400kV transmission-line design, route optimization, construction, stringing, and grid synchronization. Project Leadership: Ability to manage complex, multidisciplinary projects from development through commissioning. Commercial Acumen: Strong contract negotiation, EPC/FIDIC knowledge, claims management, and budget-control capabilities. Stakeholder Management: Strong negotiation and relationship-management skills with government authorities, landowners, communities, utilities, consultants, and contractors. Strategic Thinking: Ability to translate organizational objectives into practical project and departmental strategies. Problem Solving: Strong ability to identify project risks and implement timely mitigation measures. Communication: Excellent leadership, communication, reporting, and executive presentation skills. Mobility: Willingness to travel frequently to construction sites, remote project locations, and transmission-line alignments.

review_candidates.description: This position is on-site based in Damascus Governorate, Syria. Position Objective: Own end-to-end fibre network planning for the project of a long-distance network. Plan and validate fibre network routes, topology, capacity, splicing, ODF connectivity, route diversity, and implementation-ready fibre records for the project, ensuring alignment with service requirements and downstream transport/IP planning needs. Perform capacity planning, fibre core allocation, and utilisation forecasting across the network and ensure good Fiber planning deliverable acceptance rate. Analyse existing fibre inventory, GIS records, duct/route data, ODF records, splice diagrams, and field survey outputs to identify gaps and constraints. Prepare route plans, fiber allocation plans, cable and core utilisation views, ODF/patching requirements, and diversity assessments. Support reconciliation of planned fiber records with physical inventory, as-built documentation, and circuit data. Maintain planning trackers and deliver clean datasets for inventory update, implementation, and reporting. Strong stakeholder management and practical communication with technical and non-technical teams. High attention to detail, quality mindset, and structured documentation habits. Ability to work under delivery pressure while maintaining accuracy and governance. Strong problem-solving skills and ownership of assigned deliverables. Collaborative mindset across planning, engineering, operations, rollout, and vendor teams. Proficiency in both Arabic and English is mandatory. Qualifications & Experience: Bachelor's degree in Telecommunications, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 8+ years of experience in fiber network planning, OSP/ISP design or fibre inventory engineering. Experience with telecom GIS, fiber inventory platforms, network design tools, and structured planning datasets. Hands-on experience on route planning, diversity, and capacity planning. Experience working with multi-site field teams, contractors, and implementation vendors. Fluency in both Arabic and English is mandatory. Fiber optic design and/or installation certification preferred. FTTx/OSP planning certification preferred. GIS or telecom inventory platform training is an advantage.
